subject: Validation: garbage numbers gone, sample floor active - and a C2.2 failure I first blamed on myself was a checker auditing three runs as one
body:
Validation run finished on the fixed build. Two of the four fixes are confirmed working, one
was not exercised, and I found a defect in one of my own checkers that I had first blamed on my own
code.

CONFIRMED WORKING:

The garbage validation number is gone. Phase 3B was printing its win rate as minus 6.5 times ten to
the thirty; every line now carries a bounded number. That was an uninitialised struct being copied
wholesale over a correctly-zeroed one.

The 500-bar sample floor is active, and its cost is now visible. All nine regimes complete in zero
seconds at zero percent, because no regime accumulates 500 training bars in a one-month window. That
is the fix working as designed, not a fault - and it is the honest consequence of refusing to fit six
free parameters on about a hundred bars. It is also exactly why you were seeing a regime train at
96.5% and validate at 100%, and another train at 61.5% and validate at 0%.

NOT EXERCISED: the new threshold line never appeared, because the bar-event never fired in this run -
the whole window is consumed by calibration and its retries. That is not evidence against it, just an
untested path.

THE PART WORTH READING. The board showed C2.2 dropping from met to not met right after my edits, and
my first instinct was that I had broken it with a format-string change. I had not. The audit was
failing on DUPLICATES, and the duplicates were block numbers 1 to 8 appearing three times - because
your live log is append-only across sessions. Block 1 appears at Aug 31 23:42, Sep 2 19:06 and Sep 2
20:09, with eight EA-init boundaries in one file. The checker was auditing the whole file as though it
were a single run.

Its own documentation already said "a sequence audit across two runs is meaningless". Its only defence
was checking the build id - which cannot separate two runs of the SAME build, and every run here is
the same build. The right rule was written down and a weaker one was enforced.

It now splits the log on run boundaries and audits the newest run that actually produced blocks.
Inside that run the sequence is clean - starts at 1, no gaps, no duplicates. The self-tests that plant
a deliberate gap and a deliberate duplicate still pass, so nothing was weakened to get there.

And C2.2 is still NOT awarded, which is correct. The verdict is now "partial run": the sequence is
sound, but no completed run exists in the current log, and the criterion says "in a full run". I am
not awarding it on a prefix.

Nineteen clean compiles today. Everything saved to the ledger and to memory.
